status_summary: No executive order or law that names critical race theory training was found. Executive Order 14151 of 2025-01-20 (90 FR 8339) directs agencies to end equity-related grants and contracts to the extent allowed by law, has OPM review and revise federal training policies, and has agencies list contractors that provided DEI training to agency employees. An OPM memorandum of 2025-02-05 told agencies to end DEIA initiatives and described race-separated inclusion training as unlawful. Executive Order 14173 of 2025-01-21 (90 FR 8633) requires contract and grant terms certifying that recipients run no DEI programs that violate anti-discrimination law, and Executive Order 14398 of 2026-03-26 (91 FR 16147) requires a contract clause barring racially discriminatory DEI activities, which reaches training only through its definition of program participation. None of the three orders uses the term critical race theory, and no statute was found.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14151 (90 FR 8339, published 2025-01-29) directs agencies in section 2(b)(i) to end equity-related grants and contracts to the extent allowed by law, directs OPM in section 2(a) to review and revise training policies, and requires in section 2(b)(ii)(B) a list to OMB of contractors that provided DEI training to agency employees.

Executive Order 14173 (90 FR 8633, published 2025-01-31) requires in section 3(b)(iv) contract and grant terms making compliance with anti-discrimination law material for False Claims Act purposes and certifying no DEI programs that violate such law; the order does not mention training.

OPM issued further guidance to agencies on ending DEIA offices, programs and initiatives; it names training among covered employment actions, states that an inclusion training separating participants by race is unlawful, sets no deadlines and does not use the term critical race theory.

Executive Order 14398 (91 FR 16147, signed 2026-03-26, published 2026-03-31) requires in section 3 a contract and subcontract clause barring racially discriminatory DEI activities, with False Claims Act materiality; section 2(b) includes training programs in its definition of program participation.

title: Bar federal funding of critical race theory training by executive order and law
uncertainties: The three orders were fetched and re-read in review, and that reading reported the training provisions and confirmed that the phrase critical race theory does not appear in any of them; the text was not read line by line. A first-term order on race and sex stereotyping in training is a pre-2025 action and is not counted. Overlap: c00-01 tracks the deletion of DEI and related terms from rules, contracts and grants and cites the same orders for that purpose; c18-01 tracks the rescission of Executive Order 11246; c04-03 tracks DEI and critical race theory training at DOD; c00-06 tracks school curricula. None of these covers a government-wide ban on federally funded training of this kind, so the record is kept. The Title VII enforcement element is excluded here because it is tracked in c17-03 and c18-14. Whether OPM ended DEI training for federal employees under the order was not verified. Searches run: one web search by the researcher (first-term coverage, not cited), plus Federal Register fetches; no web search in review. Court challenges to the orders are not assessed here. On 2026-10-18 the three orders were re-read through the Federal Register web text and API (numbers, signing dates, citations and section numbers confirmed; text is an unofficial rendition). The OPM memorandum of 2025-02-05 was read; other OPM memoranda were not located, and whether OPM ended DEI training for federal employees remains unverified.
